new_task_1.title: Preserve datetime-like variables in dataset and groupby numeric reductions
new_task_1.description: Dataset reductions and grouped reductions that use the library's numeric-only filtering now treat datetime-like variables as aggregatable instead of dropping them. In practice, operations such as `groupby_bins(...).mean()` on a Dataset now retain `datetime64`, `timedelta64`, and cftime-backed variables alongside numeric variables, instead of silently omitting them from the result.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Dataset and GroupBy reduction paths that rely on numeric-only variable filtering no longer exclude datetime-like variables. Previously, the filter only accepted numeric and boolean dtypes, so grouped means and similar reductions could silently drop datetime-valued variables such as timestamps, even though those variables support aggregation semantics.

expectation.grounded: The dtype predicate used by Dataset reduction logic and GroupBy variable filtering must treat the following as aggregatable: numeric dtypes, boolean, `datetime64`, `timedelta64`, and object arrays containing cftime datetimes. The shared helper `_is_numeric_aggregatable_dtype(var)` must be used in both `xarray.core.dataset.Dataset` reduction filtering and `xarray.core.groupby.GroupBy` variable filtering so these code paths stay consistent.
expectation.conceptual: When users compute means or other numeric-style reductions on Datasets that also contain time-like variables, those time-like variables should remain in the reduced result whenever the operation is semantically valid, rather than being dropped just because they are not plain numeric arrays.

constraints.grounded: The change must not broaden aggregation eligibility beyond the explicitly supported families: numeric, boolean, numpy datetime64, numpy timedelta64, and cftime-backed datetime-like object arrays. Non-aggregatable object or string variables must still be excluded by the same filtering logic. The behavior of the underlying aggregation itself must remain unchanged; only variable selection for reduction is broadened.
constraints.conceptual: This is a filtering fix, not a redefinition of reduction semantics. Variables that genuinely cannot participate in the reduction must still be omitted or raise as before.

behavior: Dataset reduction code paths that use numeric-only filtering now consider `datetime64` variables aggregatable.
Dataset reduction code paths that use numeric-only filtering now consider `timedelta64` variables aggregatable.
Dataset reduction code paths that use numeric-only filtering now consider cftime-backed object arrays aggregatable.
GroupBy reductions use the same datetime-aware aggregatable-dtype check, so datetime-like variables are no longer silently dropped from grouped reduction results.
A grouped mean over a Dataset containing both numeric measurements and a timestamp variable preserves both outputs, and the timestamp variable retains a datetime dtype in the result.
acceptance_criteria: When a Dataset contains both a numeric variable and a `datetime64[ns]` variable, calling `groupby_bins(...).mean()` should keep both variables in the output.
When the preserved time variable is reduced through `groupby_bins(...).mean()`, its dtype in the result should remain a datetime dtype rather than being converted to object or omitted.
When a Dataset contains a `timedelta64` variable, dataset/groupby reduction paths using numeric-only filtering should include that variable rather than dropping it.
When a Dataset contains a cftime-backed datetime variable stored in an object array, dataset/groupby reduction paths using numeric-only filtering should include that variable rather than dropping it.
When a Dataset contains non-aggregatable non-datetime object variables, those variables should still be excluded from numeric reduction outputs.

new_task_2.title: Omit empty composite groups from `GroupBy.groups` for multi-grouper operations
new_task_2.description: When grouping with multiple groupers, the public `.groups` mapping no longer includes entries for cartesian-product groups that contain no members. Empty groups were previously exposed in the mapping, which made `len(groups.groups)` and iteration over group keys report combinations that never occurred in the data.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `GroupBy.groups` for multi-grouper operations only reports groups that actually contain observations. Previously, empty combinations produced by the encoded grouper state could appear in `.groups`, causing the public mapping to include zero-length groups that were not present in the underlying data.

expectation.grounded: When `GroupBy.groups` is materialized from `self.encoded.unique_coord.data` and `self.encoded.group_indices`, it must filter out empty index collections before constructing the dictionary. The resulting mapping should only contain keys whose corresponding grouped index sequence is non-empty.
expectation.conceptual: Users inspecting `.groups` should see only real groups that exist in the input data, not placeholder combinations generated by multi-grouper bookkeeping.

constraints.grounded: The fix applies to the exposed `.groups` mapping and must not alter the definition of non-empty groups, the ordering of real groups, or the grouping behavior for actual observations. Single-grouper and normal non-empty group behavior must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: This should clean up the public group listing without changing how data are assigned to valid groups.

behavior: For multi-grouper operations, `.groups` excludes group combinations whose index list is empty.
The number of entries in `.groups` now matches the number of realized groups in the data rather than the number of encoded candidate combinations.
Iterating over `.groups` no longer yields empty-bin keys that have no matching rows.
acceptance_criteria: When grouping a Dataset with multiple groupers where some grouper combinations do not occur in the data, `len(groups.groups)` should count only the combinations that do occur.
When inspecting `groups.groups` after a multi-grouper operation, no key should map to an empty index collection.
When all realized groups are non-empty, the keys and member indices in `.groups` should otherwise remain unchanged from prior behavior.

new_task_3.title: Fix `to_dataframe()` for single-dimension MultiIndexes and preserve coordinate dtypes
new_task_3.description: DataArray and Dataset conversion to pandas DataFrames now exclude index coordinates, rather than excluding only dimension names, when deciding which variables become DataFrame columns. This fixes cases where a MultiIndex on a single xarray dimension previously caused its component index coordinates to be duplicated as both index levels and columns. The conversion path also preserves coordinate/index level dtypes more faithfully when building pandas MultiIndexes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `DataArray.to_dataframe()` and `Dataset.to_dataframe()` do not duplicate index coordinates as DataFrame columns when the xarray object uses a MultiIndex along a single dimension. Previously, the conversion excluded only dimension names, so component coordinates of a single-dimension MultiIndex could appear both in the DataFrame index and again as ordinary columns, breaking equality with the corresponding Series/DataFrame representation and making `reset_index()` produce duplicate columns. Coordinate and index level dtypes should also be preserved during the conversion.

expectation.grounded: The DataFrame conversion path in `Dataset._to_dataframe()` must build `columns_in_order` by excluding names present in `self.xindexes`, not merely names present in `self.dims`. This ensures that all index arrays, including MultiIndex component coordinates, are omitted from the output columns. MultiIndex construction in coordinates handling must preserve pandas level objects rather than coercing them through Python lists, so pandas index level dtypes remain intact.
expectation.conceptual: When an xarray object is converted to a pandas DataFrame, index coordinates should live only in the pandas index, never be duplicated as data columns, and dtype information for coordinates should survive the round-trip into pandas as accurately as possible.

constraints.grounded: Non-index coordinates should continue to be emitted as DataFrame columns. Existing column ordering for real non-index variables must remain intact. The fix must specifically avoid duplicating MultiIndex component coordinates while preserving unrelated scalar or derived coordinates as columns.
constraints.conceptual: This is a correctness fix for pandas conversion, not a redesign of xarray's indexing model. Objects without index-coordinate duplication issues should continue to produce the same DataFrame structure as before.

behavior: When a DataArray is indexed by a MultiIndex along a single dimension, `to_dataframe()` now matches `to_series().to_frame()` instead of adding duplicate index-coordinate columns.
When a Dataset has a MultiIndex along a single dimension, `to_dataframe()` places the MultiIndex levels only in the DataFrame index, not again in the columns.
Calling `reset_index()` on the resulting DataFrame no longer creates duplicate columns for the MultiIndex level names.
Other non-index coordinates remain available as ordinary DataFrame columns.
Coordinate and MultiIndex level dtypes are preserved more faithfully during DataFrame conversion.
acceptance_criteria: When converting a single-dimension MultiIndexed DataArray to a DataFrame, the result should be equal to `to_series().to_frame()`.
When converting a single-dimension MultiIndexed Dataset to a DataFrame, the MultiIndex component coordinates should appear only in the DataFrame index and not as duplicate columns.
When `reset_index()` is applied to the DataFrame from the previous case, it should succeed without duplicate-column collisions and produce the expected tabular result.
When a Dataset includes additional non-index coordinates alongside a single-dimension MultiIndex, those non-index coordinates should still appear as columns in the DataFrame output.
When coordinate arrays use specific numeric dtypes, the corresponding DataFrame columns or index levels should preserve those dtypes after conversion.
